title: Have an agent shop in a phone app and stop before paying
summary: A poster describes a PhoneUse demo where an agent opened Amazon on a real cloud phone, added a 12-pack of Diet Coke and stopped at the $8.87 order review.
agent_role: The agent opened the app, searched, picked the product and moved through the cart to the order screen. The human keeps the final 'Place your order' tap.
outcome: The poster reports the demo reached order review with an $8.87 total and stopped before buying.
what_they_did: The poster shares a demo of PhoneUse, a service that gives an agent a real Android or iPhone in the cloud. The agent was asked to find a 12-pack of Diet Coke on Amazon and go to order review. It opened the app, searched, picked the pack and walked the cart to the order sheet.
how_it_went: The poster says it reached an $8.87 total and stopped on 'Place your order', leaving payment to the human. The launch also showed Uber rides, TikTok trend research and an old insurance app.
worth_knowing: Read each app's terms first. The poster notes Amazon is blocking shopping agents and some apps clearly don't want agents inside them.
prompt: Using a phone I give you access to, open [shopping app] and find [item and size]. Add it to the cart and go to the order review screen. Show me the item, quantity and total price. Do not place the order or enter any payment details; stop there and wait for me to tap the final button myself.

curation.rationale: A launch-style post for PhoneUse with one concrete demo: an agent shops in the real Amazon phone app and stops before payment. It is promotional and relays someone else's launch, but it shows a specific multi-step task.
